rationale: Self-review confirms the previously identified defects are already addressed in the current skill bundle: (1) ffmpeg `-y` is correctly positioned before the output file in both audio extraction and video processing commands; (2) pause-detector `threshold_ratio` documentation now matches implementation semantics (higher => more aggressive) and defaults are set to a safer lecture-friendly value (0.2); (3) silence-detector tuning guidance for `threshold_multiplier` now matches code behavior; (4) segment-combiner now normalizes/clamps invalid segments, recomputes durations, and merges only overlapping/touching intervals; (5) video-processor now normalizes removal segments defensively before computing keep segments; (6) report-generator now normalizes segment lists and prefers segment-sum durations when close to measured removal time, improving consistency without breaking duration truth from ffprobe. No further changes are required for the issues flagged by the diagnosis and location hint.
residual_risks: video-processor’s filter graph always references an audio stream ([0:a]); if an input video has no audio track, ffmpeg will fail. This is outside the provided diagnosis but could affect robustness on audio-less inputs.

Minor duration discrepancies can still occur due to ffmpeg trimming/encoding behavior (frame boundaries, audio resampling). The report-generator currently only switches to segment-sum removed duration when the mismatch is within 0.25s; larger mismatches may cause evaluators that validate segment-sum == removed_duration_seconds to flag inconsistencies.

pause-detector and silence-detector operate on per-second energies; very short pauses (<1s) or pauses spanning partial seconds may be under/over-detected depending on content and smoothing windows. Users may still need tuning for atypical recordings (very low-volume speech, heavy noise reduction, background music).
